content: 1. Bacteriostatic agents may interfere with the bactericidal effects of ceftriaxone due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these agents. 2. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate reduces the efficacy of cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents can inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 3. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A4 substrates when co-administered with cenobamate. 4. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate elevates the levels or effects of cevimeline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Ciprofloxacin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration with drugs that prolong the QT interval may increase the risk of torsades de pointes in predisposed patients. However, this risk is lower with ciprofloxacin compared to other quinolones. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases citalopram levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. ECG monitoring is recommended, especially when co-administered with drugs that may prolong the QT interval. 9. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases clarithromycin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases conivaptan levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. 12. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases cortisone levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases crizotinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Crizotinib also increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels. Dose reduction may be necessary for co-administered drugs metabolized predominantly by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Crofelemer increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and transporters MRP2 and OATP1A2 in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases cyclosporine levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Cyclosporine also increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dabigatran levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 18. Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dactinomycin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Danazol increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Danicopan increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dapsone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases daridorexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Daridorexant dose should not exceed 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Dasatinib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases daunorubicin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Deferasirox decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases deflazacort levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Deutetrabenazine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dexamethasone levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases diazepam levels (both buccal and intranasal forms) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 33. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases digoxin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases disopyramide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases docetaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Dolasetron and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases donepezil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases doxorubicin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases doxorubicin liposomal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dutasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Duvelisib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration increases the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing toxicity risks. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates and monitor for signs of toxicity. 42. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Elagolix increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider dose adjustments as needed. 44. Eliglustat increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of the P-gp substrate and titrate to clinical effect. 45. Eluxadoline increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by decreasing metabolism. Eluxadoline may also increase systemic exposure of co-administered OATP1B1 substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious or life-threatening events. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Encorafenib affects erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Encorafenib may also increase the concentration and toxicity of OATP1B3 substrates. Monitor closely for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments. 48. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases eplerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases erlotinib levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases estradiol levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases esterified estrogens levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases esterified estrogens levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases estropipate levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases estropipate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases eszopiclone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the eszopiclone starting dose to 1 mg/day. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 59. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases etoposide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases eucalyptus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases exemestane levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ezogabine both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
